documents.document_title: The Consumer Protection (Mediation) Rules, 2020

documents.notes: Official consumer authority guidelines on misleading advertisements.

documents.document_title: The Legal Metrology Act, 2009
documents.notes: Weights and measures, MRP as a ceiling, mandatory net-quantity and package declarations, verification of weighing/measuring instruments, and related offences and penalties. Substantive basis for overcharging-above-MRP and short-weight complaints.

documents.document_title: The Legal Metrology (Packaged Commodities) Rules, 2011
documents.notes: Pre-packaged goods: mandatory label declarations (manufacturer/packer, net quantity, MRP inclusive of all taxes, month/year, consumer-care, country of origin), dual-MRP prohibition, maximum permissible error, and penalties.

documents.document_title: The Sale of Goods Act, 1930
documents.notes: Supporting contract-law background for defective-goods reasoning: implied conditions and warranties, merchantable quality, sale by description/sample, passing of property and risk, delivery, and buyer/seller remedies. Not a consumer-forum statute; use alongside the Consumer Protection Act.

documents.document_title: The Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 2016
documents.notes: Standard Mark / ISI certification, compulsory conformity assessment for notified goods, hallmarking, product recall powers, and penalties for non-conforming or falsely marked goods.

documents.document_title: The Insurance Ombudsman Rules, 2017 (updated to 18 May 2021)
documents.notes: Remedy route for insurance claim repudiation, delay, mis-selling and policy-servicing disputes: Ombudsman jurisdiction, monetary limit, complaint procedure, award and time limits. Consolidated text incorporating the 2018/2021 amendments.

documents.document_title: The Reserve Bank - Integrated Ombudsman Scheme, 2021 (with 2022 amendments)
documents.notes: Cost-free remedy for deficiency in banking, NBFC and digital-payment services (subsumes the earlier Banking / NBFC / Digital Transactions ombudsman schemes). Grounds unauthorised-transaction and payment-service complaints; document_type set to guidelines because ingest.py has no scheme parser.

documents.document_title: The Information Technology Act, 2000
documents.notes: Core cyber law statute.

documents.document_title: The Information Technology (Intermediary Guidelines and Digital Media Ethics Code) Rules, 2021
documents.notes: Rules for intermediaries and digital media under the IT Act.

documents.document_title: The Digital Personal Data Protection Rules, 2025
documents.notes: Rules made under the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023; the Act itself is not present as a standalone PDF.

documents.document_title: User Manual for Reporting Cyber Crime Against Women and Children / Citizen Manual for National Cybercrime Reporting Portal
documents.short_title: National Cybercrime Reporting Portal User Manual, 2019
documents.notes: Procedural guide, not a statute or rule.

documents.document_title: The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023
documents.notes: Broad criminal law retained as supporting material for cyber-adjacent offences (identity, cheating by personation, obscenity, voyeurism, stalking, extortion, criminal intimidation). Candidate for replacement by a curated cyber-sections extract to cut retrieval noise.

documents.document_title: The Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023
documents.notes: Primary data-protection statute (No. 22 of 2023). Pairs with the DPDP Rules, 2025 already in the corpus.

documents.document_title: The Information Technology (Reasonable Security Practices and Procedures and Sensitive Personal Data or Information) Rules, 2011
documents.notes: Body-corporate data-security and sensitive-personal-data obligations under IT Act s.43A.

documents.document_title: The Information Technology (Procedure and Safeguards for Blocking for Access of Information by Public) Rules, 2009
documents.notes: Government process for blocking unlawful online content under IT Act s.69A; relevant to takedown of NCII and unlawful material.

documents.document_title: The Information Technology (Procedure and Safeguards for Interception, Monitoring and Decryption of Information) Rules, 2009
documents.notes: Lawful interception, monitoring and decryption safeguards under IT Act s.69; supporting context.

documents.document_title: CERT-In Directions under sub-section (6) of section 70B of the Information Technology Act, 2000, dated 28 April 2022
documents.notes: Mandatory cyber-incident reporting (six-hour window) and log-retention directions issued by CERT-In.

documents.document_title: Reserve Bank of India - Customer Protection - Limiting Liability of Customers in Unauthorised Electronic Banking Transactions (DBR.No.Leg.BC.78/09.07.005/2017-18, 6 July 2017)
documents.notes: Zero and limited customer liability plus reporting and credit-back timelines for unauthorised electronic banking and online payment fraud.

documents.document_title: The Information Technology (Intermediary Guidelines and Digital Media Ethics Code) Amendment Rules, 2023
documents.notes: Amends the 2021 Intermediary Rules (online gaming intermediaries, fact-check unit, due-diligence changes). The 2022 amendment is not yet in the corpus.

documents.document_title: National Payments Corporation of India - Unified Payments Interface (UPI) Procedural Guidelines
documents.notes: UPI dispute-redressal and chargeback mechanics. Mirror copy; verify version and date before production use.

documents.document_title: National Cyber Crime Reporting Portal - Citizen User Manual (reporting cyber crimes other than child sexual abuse material)
documents.short_title: National Cybercrime Reporting Portal Citizen Manual
documents.notes: MHA / I4C portal manual covering financial fraud, SIM-swap, e-wallet, ransomware reporting and the 1930 helpline. Supplements the 2019 women and children manual.

documents.document_title: Sanchar Saathi / CEIR - Citizen User Manual (blocking a lost or stolen mobile, SIM verification, fraud reporting)
documents.notes: Department of Telecommunications portal guide: block a lost or stolen phone (CEIR), check SIMs registered in your name (TAFCOP), report fraud communications (Chakshu).

documents.document_title: The Information Technology (Intermediary Guidelines and Digital Media Ethics Code) Amendment Rules, 2022
documents.notes: G.S.R. 794(E), 28 Oct 2022. Introduces Grievance Appellate Committees (appeal against an intermediary's Grievance Officer within 30 days) and updated terms-of-use/privacy-policy duties. Sits between the base 2021 rules and the 2023 amendment already in the corpus.

documents.document_title: The Delhi Rent Control Act, 1958
documents.notes: Core Delhi rent-control statute. Consolidated text as amended up to the Delhi Rent Control (Amendment) Act, 1988 (Act 57 of 1988): s.3(c) excludes premises let at monthly rent above Rs. 3,500, and s.3(d) excludes premises for 10 years from completion of construction, so most present-day Delhi tenancies fall outside this Act and are governed by contract and the Transfer of Property Act, 1882. Key provisions: standard rent (s.4-9), protection against eviction and grounds (s.14), bona-fide-need summary procedure (s.25B), deposit of rent with the Controller (s.26-28), landlord's duty to repair (s.44), and cutting off essential supply or service (s.45).

documents.document_title: The Delhi Rent Control Rules, 1959
documents.notes: Rules under the Delhi Rent Control Act, 1958.

documents.document_title: The Delhi Rent Act, 1995
documents.notes: Enacted but its commencement notification was never issued, so it has never been brought into force and is not operative law. The Delhi Rent Control Act, 1958 remains the governing rent-control statute for Delhi. Retained for reference only; do not cite its provisions as applicable law.

documents.document_title: The Transfer of Property Act, 1882
documents.notes: Supporting property law relevant to leases and transfers.

documents.document_title: The Registration Act, 1908
documents.notes: Supporting document-registration law relevant to lease and property documents.

documents.document_title: The Specific Relief Act, 1963
documents.notes: Supporting civil-remedy statute. s.6: a person dispossessed of immovable property without consent and otherwise than in due course of law may sue to recover possession within six months (no such suit against the Government); s.5 recovery of possession on title; s.38-39 perpetual and mandatory injunctions to restrain or undo interference. Core remedy for illegal lockout or forcible eviction by a landlord. Original 1963 text; later amendments (Act 18 of 2018) not reflected.

documents.document_title: The Indian Easements Act, 1882
documents.notes: Supporting property law. s.52 defines a licence (a right to use another's immovable property that is not a lease or interest in land); s.60 licence revocability and the exception for a licensee who has acted on it with permanent works; s.62-64 deemed revocation and the licensee's rights on revocation or eviction. Relevant to distinguishing a tenant from a paying-guest / licensee, who has weaker protection. The Delhi Rent Control Act, 1958 expressly excludes a s.52 licensee from the definition of tenant.

documents.document_title: The Slum Areas (Improvement and Clearance) Act, 1956
documents.notes: Applies to declared slum areas in Union territories including Delhi. s.19: no suit or proceeding for eviction of a tenant from a building or land in a slum area may be instituted (or an existing decree executed) without the competent authority's prior written permission, which turns on whether alternative accommodation within the tenant's means is available; s.20 appeal to the Administrator. Preserved by DRC Act 1958 s.54. Does not apply to premises belonging to the Government, DDA or a local authority (s.21). Consolidated text incl. the 1964 amendment.

documents.document_title: The Indian Stamp Act, 1899 (as amended)
documents.notes: Stamp duty framework, including Schedule I Article 35 (Lease) — the basis for stamp duty on rent/lease agreements. Central Act applicable in Delhi (no separate Delhi Stamp Act). Distinct from the archived Uttarakhand-specific copy in archive/.

documents.document_title: The Constitution of India
documents.notes: Core constitutional source.

documents.document_title: The Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993
documents.notes: Public-authority and human-rights institutional statute. Consolidated text as amended up to the Protection of Human Rights (Amendment) Act, 2019 (Act 19 of 2019).

documents.document_title: The Legal Services Authorities Act, 1987
documents.notes: Core statute for legal aid services.

documents.document_title: The Right to Information Act, 2005
documents.notes: Primary public-authority transparency statute; references to DPDP amendments do not make this the DPDP Act.

documents.document_title: The Contempt of Courts Act, 1971
documents.notes: Specialized court-authority statute.

documents.document_title: The Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education Act, 2009
documents.notes: Article 21A implementation: free and compulsory elementary education for children aged 6-14; decentralised grievance redressal to local authority and State Commission for Protection of Child Rights. Consolidated text as amended up to Act 1 of 2019.

documents.document_title: The Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016
documents.short_title: Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016
documents.notes: Rights and entitlements of persons with disabilities against public authorities: equality and non-discrimination, accessibility duties, reservation, Grievance Redressal Officers in every Government establishment, Chief/State Commissioners, and Special Courts.

documents.document_title: The Maintenance and Welfare of Parents and Senior Citizens Act, 2007
documents.notes: Citizen entitlement enforced through public Maintenance Tribunals and Appellate Tribunals: monthly maintenance from children/relatives, protection of life and property, revocation of property transfers, old-age homes. No legal practitioner permitted before the Tribunal.

documents.document_title: The Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act, 2013
documents.notes: Anti-corruption grievance mechanism against public servants: Lokpal for the Union and Lokayukta for States, complaint procedure, preliminary inquiry and investigation, Special Courts, and penalty for false complaints. Consolidated text as amended up to Act 37 of 2016.

documents.document_title: The Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988
documents.notes: Core statute on bribery and criminal misconduct by public servants: offences, Special Judges, prior sanction for prosecution (s.19) and prior approval for inquiry (s.17A). Consolidated text as amended up to the Prevention of Corruption (Amendment) Act, 2018 (Act 16 of 2018).

documents.document_title: The Administrative Tribunals Act, 1985
documents.notes: Article 323-A adjudication of public-service recruitment and conditions-of-service disputes by the Central Administrative Tribunal and State Administrative Tribunals: applications under s.19, exhaustion of remedies (s.20), limitation (s.21), right to a legal practitioner (s.23). Consolidated text as amended up to Act 1 of 2007.

documents.document_title: The Commissions for Protection of Child Rights Act, 2005
documents.short_title: Commissions for Protection of Child Rights Act, 2005
documents.notes: Constitutes the National Commission and State Commissions for Protection of Child Rights: functions (s.13), civil-court powers of inquiry into complaints of deprivation or violation of child rights (s.14), steps after inquiry incl. recommending prosecution and approaching the High Court/Supreme Court (s.15), and Children's Courts (s.25). This is the body the Right to Education Act, 2009 s.31-32 routes child-education grievances to. Consolidated text incl. Act 4 of 2007.

documents.document_title: The Right to Information Rules, 2012
documents.notes: Central rules under s.27 of the RTI Act, 2005 (G.S.R. 603(E)), superseding the 2005 fee and appeal-procedure rules. r.3 Rs. 10 application fee (max 500 words); r.4 fee schedule for copies, inspection (first hour free, Rs. 5/hour thereafter) and postal charges; r.5 no fee for a person below the poverty line; r.6 modes of payment; r.8 second appeal to the Central Information Commission with the format of appeal in the Appendix; rr.9-15 return, process, hearing and disposal of the second appeal. Governs Central public authorities; States have their own RTI rules.

documents.document_title: The National Legal Services Authority (Free and Competent Legal Services) Regulations, 2010
documents.short_title: NALSA (Free and Competent Legal Services) Regulations, 2010
documents.notes: Regulations under s.29 of the Legal Services Authorities Act, 1987 governing how free legal aid is actually applied for and delivered. reg.3 application for legal services (Form-I, oral/e-mail requests accepted); reg.4 front office; reg.5 a self-certificate that the applicant falls within s.12 of the Act is ordinarily sufficient proof of entitlement; reg.7 scrutiny and a decision within seven days, with an appeal to the Executive Chairman; reg.8 empanelment, assignment and honorarium of panel and retainer lawyers; reg.10-12 Monitoring and Mentoring Committees; reg.13 financial assistance for court fees and copies. As amended up to 2019.

documents.document_title: The National Legal Services Authority (Legal Services Clinics) Regulations, 2011
documents.notes: Regulations under s.29 of the Legal Services Authorities Act, 1987 for District Legal Services Authority legal services clinics (Village Legal Care and Support Centres) as the first point of contact for legal help. reg.3 establishment in villages, jails, protection homes and other areas of barriered access; reg.4 eligibility is the s.12 criteria; reg.5-10 para-legal volunteers and deputed panel/retainer lawyers, including help drafting petitions and applications for MGNREGA job cards, identity documents and other Government-scheme benefits; reg.16-18 amicable settlement and referral to Lok Adalats. As amended in 2014.

documents.document_title: The National Legal Services Authority (Lok Adalats) Regulations, 2009
documents.notes: Regulations under s.29 of the Legal Services Authorities Act, 1987 on organising Lok Adalats. reg.6 composition of benches; reg.10 reference of pending cases (s.20 of the Act / s.89 CPC) and of pre-litigation matters, with non-compoundable criminal cases and contested divorce excluded; reg.13 members act as statutory conciliators only, cannot coerce a settlement, and cannot grant bail or divorce by mutual consent; reg.17 the signed settlement becomes an award (deemed a civil-court decree, final, no appeal) and any court fee paid is refunded; reg.18 confidentiality. As amended up to 2019.

They are excluded from ingest.py because judgments need a dedicated judgment parser (headnote / holding / ratio) and good-law metadata. Move them into 'documents' only after that parser exists.

pending_case_law.case_name: Shreya Singhal v. Union of India
pending_case_law.notes: Struck down IT Act s.66A; upheld s.69A with safeguards; read down s.79(3)(b) intermediary safe harbour. The assistant must never cite s.66A as valid law.

pending_case_law.case_name: Justice K.S. Puttaswamy (Retd) v. Union of India
pending_case_law.notes: Right to privacy is a fundamental right under Article 21; basis for personal-data-misuse claims.

pending_case_law.case_name: Anuradha Bhasin v. Union of India
pending_case_law.notes: Internet access is protected under Article 19(1)(a); restrictions and shutdowns must be necessary, proportionate, published and reviewable.

pending_case_law.case_name: Mrs X v. Union of India
pending_case_law.notes: Non-consensual intimate images: intermediaries must proactively remove all instances, not only user-supplied URLs; directions to MeitY and Delhi Police; cybercrime-portal status tracker.

pending_case_law.case_name: Subhranshu Rout @ Gugul v. State of Odisha
pending_case_law.notes: Right to be forgotten within Article 21; a victim's right to have objectionable images removed from social media. Bail order with extended discussion.

pending_case_law.case_name: Sharat Babu Digumarti v. Government (NCT of Delhi)
pending_case_law.notes: The IT Act is a special law and displaces general IPC/BNS provisions for obscene content in electronic form (s.67 / s.79 context).

pending_case_law.case_name: Indian Medical Association v. V.P. Shantha
pending_case_law.notes: Held that medical services rendered for consideration fall within 'service' under the Consumer Protection Act; medical negligence complaints are maintainable before consumer fora. Foundational for whether a professional/medical service dispute belongs in the consumer forum.

pending_case_law.case_name: Lucknow Development Authority v. M.K. Gupta
pending_case_law.notes: Statutory/development authorities are 'service providers' under the Act; deficiency in housing/possession delay attracts compensation for harassment and mental agony, not merely a refund. Basis for compensation-beyond-refund reasoning in delayed-possession disputes.

pending_case_law.case_name: Experion Developers Pvt. Ltd. v. Sushma Ashok Shiroor
pending_case_law.citation: Civil Appeal No. 6044 of 2019, decided 7 April 2022
pending_case_law.notes: Consumer Protection Act and RERA remedies are concurrent, not mutually exclusive — a homebuyer is not confined to RERA. Builder must refund the full amount paid, with interest, for possession delayed beyond the agreed timeline. Key precedent for builder-delay refund disputes.

pending_case_law.case_name: Rohit Chaudhary v. M/S Vipul Ltd.
pending_case_law.notes: Clarifies the 'commercial purpose' exclusion under s.2(7) of the Consumer Protection Act, 2019 (s.2(1)(d) of the 1986 Act): a purchase made for self-employment/livelihood is not automatically excluded as 'commercial purpose'. Fact-specific test, not a rigid formula — relevant whenever a complainant's consumer status is disputed because the goods/services were bought for business use.
